newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast products weaker in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast products weaker in thin trade.

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot refined products prices were pegged modestly lower, reflecting weakness rippling through the market on Tuesday's correction in NYMEX gasoline and heating oil futures, traders said.
But trade was thin in the Los Angeles and San Francisco markets as traders remained on the sidelines ahead of the weekly inventory estimates delayed by the long holiday weekend, traders said.
"I've had people call and say they are going to wait for the stats," one trader said of the American Petroleum Institute estimates delayed a day by the long holiday weekend.
NYMEX July unleaded gasoline ended the day down 1.90 cents a gallon at 63.00 cents a gallon, and heating oil fell 2.26 cents to close at 55.22 cents a gallon.

++ GASOLINE: Conventional grade gasoline eased one cent a gallon to 60/61 cents a gallon in Los Angeles. Traders pegged June CARB unleaded gasoline slightly lower at 63/64 cents a gallon in Los Angeles. Reformulated (RFG) grade for sale in Phoenix, Ariz., remained 1.50 cents under CARB.
++ DISTILLATES: June CARB diesel in L.A. was talked 64/65.50 cents a gallon, giving back Friday's modest gains. Low sulphur "EPA" diesel eased one cent to 58 cents bid, 58.50 cents asked.
